items.title: Purple/indigo/violet gradient and "AI glow"
items.detect: `from-purple-*`, `via-violet-*`, `to-indigo-*`, `linear-gradient(...)` with #6366f1 / #8b5cf6 / #7c3aed / #a855f7, colored `box-shadow` halos around buttons or cards.
items.instead: Start from the brand's own color. Use flat fills; if a gradient is earned, keep it to two close stops of the same hue, used once.

items.title: Gradient-text headlines
items.detect: `bg-clip-text text-transparent`, `-webkit-background-clip: text`.
items.instead: Solid ink color. Get emphasis from weight, size, or one highlighted word in the accent.

items.title: Glassmorphism as decoration
items.detect: `backdrop-blur*`, `backdrop-filter: blur()` on cards, navbars, and badges all at once; translucent white borders everywhere.
items.instead: Opaque surfaces separated by value (lighter or darker step) or a 1px hairline. Use blur only where content really scrolls under something (a sticky nav over imagery).

items.title: Decorative blur blobs and orbs
items.detect: absolutely positioned `rounded-full blur-3xl` divs, `filter: blur(80px)` circles behind the hero.
items.instead: Real imagery, product UI, a typographic composition, or plain space.

items.title: Cream + terracotta "AI editorial"
items.detect: background #F4F1EA / #F5F0E8 / #FAF7F2 with #C2410C / #D97757 / #CC785C accents and a generic serif display face.
items.instead: Derive warmth from the brand if it has any. If you want an editorial feel, commit to a specific typeface and grid, not the stock palette.

items.title: Neon-on-black dark mode
items.detect: #000 canvas with saturated cyan/magenta/lime glows and glowing borders.
items.instead: An off-black canvas (#0E0F11 to #16171A), 2–3 surface steps, one accent at reduced chroma, `color-scheme: dark`.

items.title: Centered hero + three equal feature cards
items.detect: centered H1/sub/two buttons, then `grid-cols-3` of icon + title + two lines, repeated down the page.
items.instead: Pick a composition from the content: left-aligned headline with product visual, split layout, a single strong statement with proof underneath, a feature list with unequal emphasis (one lead feature, smaller secondary ones).

items.title: Centered everything
items.detect: `text-center` on most sections; long paragraphs centered.
items.instead: Left-align body copy and most sections. Center only short, isolated statements.

items.title: Same rhythm for every section
items.detect: every section = small label + H2 + gray subtitle + grid. Same padding, same width.
items.instead: Vary density and width by section job (proof = dense, story = narrow and airy, pricing = tabular). See [craft § rhythm](craft.md#spacing-and-rhythm).

items.title: Cards inside cards; card stacks for everything
items.detect: bordered/shadowed containers nested 2+ deep; every piece of content boxed.
items.instead: Group with space and alignment first, then a divider, then a card only if the thing is a separate, clickable object.

items.title: Default bento grid
items.detect: a 2×3 or 3×3 mosaic of rounded tiles with icons and one-line claims, used because it is fashionable.
items.instead: Use a bento only when the tiles show real, different content (screenshots, data, quotes) of meaningfully different sizes.

items.title: Hero overlays and stickers
items.detect: floating badges ("✨ New", "🚀 v2.0"), detached labels, rotated stickers, avatars stacked with "Join 10k+".
items.instead: Put announcements in the nav or under the primary action as a plain text link. Nothing sits above the headline (see 24).

items.title: Inter/Roboto/Arial as the only display face
items.detect: one family for everything, all headings `font-bold` at roughly the same sizes.
items.instead: Choose a display face with character that fits the Design Read and pair it with a readable text face (see [craft § typography](craft.md#typography)). Inter is fine for body and UI text.

items.title: No type scale
items.detect: arbitrary sizes (`text-[37px]`, 15 different sizes), headings that barely differ from body.
items.instead: A ratio-based scale with 6–8 steps; headline at least 2.5× body on desktop.

items.title: Uniform radius + shadow on everything
items.detect: the same `rounded-2xl shadow-lg` (or `rounded-xl shadow-md`) on cards, buttons, inputs, images.
items.instead: A radius scale by role (controls small, containers medium, media square or large) and elevation only for things that float (menus, dialogs).

items.title: Icon soup
items.detect: a lucide/heroicons icon in every card, bullet, button, and heading; many icons imported in one file.
items.instead: Icons only where they speed up recognition (nav, controls, status). Feature lists can use numbers, typography, or real screenshots.

items.title: Emoji as bullets, icons, or badges
items.detect: emoji at the start of list items, headings, buttons, or badges (🚀 ✨ ⚡ 🔥 ✅).
items.instead: Real list markers, an icon from the project set, or nothing.

items.title: transition: all and unguarded motion
items.detect: `transition-all`, `transition: all`; keyframes or `animate-*` with no `prefers-reduced-motion` / `motion-safe:` / `motion-reduce:`.
items.instead: Transition named properties (`opacity, transform`), 150–300ms, and guard non-essential motion.

items.title: Removed focus outline
items.detect: `outline-none` / `outline: none` without a `focus-visible` replacement.
items.instead: `focus-visible:` ring in the accent color, offset 2px.

items.title: Generic hero and marketing copy
items.detect: "Unlock the power of", "Supercharge", "Seamless", "Elevate your", "Revolutionize", "Next-level", "Cutting-edge", "Harness", "Empower", "Effortless", "In today's fast-paced world", "Built for the future", "lorem ipsum".
items.instead: Say what the product does, for whom, with a concrete noun and number: *"Track every Pokémon Unite match you play, with per-hero win rates."*

items.title: Generic CTAs
items.detect: "Get Started", "Learn More", "View more", "Sign Up Now", "Try it free" as the only CTA text; the same link or button label under every card in a grid (six "View more" links weigh the whole block).
items.instead: Name the action and object: "Open the build wheel", "Import my matches". In lists, use one section-level action, an icon-only control with a tooltip, or reveal the control on row hover — do not repeat the same CTA label on every card.

items.title: Fake social proof and metrics
items.detect: "Trusted by 10,000+ teams", "10x faster", "99.9% uptime", testimonials from "Jane Doe, CEO at Acme", logo walls of companies that are not customers.
items.instead: Use only real, sourced proof. If none exists, leave the section out, or mark it `TODO(content): real testimonial` so it cannot ship by accident.

items.title: Stock filler content
items.detect: placeholder paragraphs that could describe any product; stock photos of people pointing at laptops; three-word feature titles ("Fast. Secure. Reliable.").
items.instead: Use the project's real content: actual screenshots, data, names, prices, changelog items. Ask for content when it is missing rather than inventing it.

items.title: Eyebrow / kicker above a heading
items.detect: a tiny uppercase, letter-spaced or pill-shaped label ("INTRODUCING", "Features", "New") on the line right before an H1–H3.
items.instead: Delete it, or put its useful words into the heading. If the page needs wayfinding, use breadcrumbs or the nav.

items.title: Decorative section numbers
items.detect: "01 — Discover", "02", "03" labels on sections that are not steps.
items.instead: Number only things the reader must do or read in order (setup steps, a process). Otherwise the heading is enough.

items.title: Hero-metric row
items.detect: three or more huge numbers with tiny captions ("99%", "2.4M", "150+"), usually right under the hero.
items.instead: Use a number only when it is real, sourced, and explains the product; give it a sentence of context. One meaningful number beats a row of vague ones.

items.title: Colored side-tab borders
items.detect: `border-left: 4px solid <color>` or `border-l-4 border-<color>` on ordinary cards, list items, or quotes.
items.instead: Keep side stripes for real status (an error or warning callout). Elsewhere separate with space or a full 1px hairline.

items.title: Bounce, elastic, or overshoot easing
items.detect: `animate-bounce`, `easeOutBack`/`elastic`, `cubic-bezier()` with a y value below 0 or above 1.
items.instead: A short ease-out that settles once. Playful springs only where the brand is explicitly playful, and never on routine UI like dialogs.

items.title: Endless attention loops
items.detect: a small `rounded-full` dot with `animate-ping`/`animate-pulse`, `<marquee>`, logo tickers that scroll forever.
items.instead: Static status stays static; animate only a real change. Logo rows sit still and can be scanned at the reader's pace.

items.title: Hard offset shadows
items.detect: `box-shadow: 6px 6px 0 #000`, `shadow-[4px_4px_0_...]` on a site that is not neobrutalist anywhere else.
items.instead: Elevation from soft, offset shadows on floating UI only, or no shadow at all. Use the hard block shadow only if the whole visual language is built on it.

items.title: Gray text on colored surfaces
items.detect: `bg-indigo-600 text-gray-400`, or neutral gray copy on any saturated panel.
items.instead: Use a light ink, or a tint of the surface's own hue for secondary text, and check contrast against the real background.

items.title: Em-dash overuse
items.detect: em dashes on four or more lines of one file's visible copy ("Fast — reliable — secure").
items.instead: Most dashes want to be a full stop. Keep a dash only where an aside really interrupts the sentence.

items.title: "Not X. A Y." slogan contrast
items.detect: "Not just another dashboard. A command center.", "It's not a tool. It's a platform."
items.instead: Say what it does in one plain sentence. If the difference from alternatives matters, name the alternative and the concrete difference.

items.title: Oversized hero headline
items.detect: the headline alone fills the first viewport; more than 3 lines at 1440px or more than 5 at 390px; the CTA falls below the fold.
items.instead: Shorten the headline first, then cap the size (see [craft § typography](craft.md#typography)).

items.title: Off-system values
items.detect: fonts, hex colors, or radii in code that are not in the project's DESIGN.md `design-tokens` block.
items.instead: Use a documented token. If the new value is intentional, add it to DESIGN.md first (and log why), then use it.

items.title: Trailing-period wordmark
items.detect: a brand or logo lockup that ends with a decorative period ("Acme.", "Linear.", "`<CYBER./>`"). Common in Claude/ChatGPT-invented marks.
items.instead: Drop the trailing dot. Periods belong in sentences, not in the name of the product.
